newsitem.title: ITALY: RALLYING - WORLD CHAMPION'S CO-DRIVER INJURED IN CRASH.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING - WORLD CHAMPION'S CO-DRIVER INJURED IN CRASH.

text.p: New world champion Tommi Makinen crashed his Mitsubishi in the San Remo Rally on Monday, injuring his co-driver, Seppo Harjanne.
Finland's Harjanne was flown to hospital with a cracked vertebra after the accident which occurred just 500 metres into the opening stage.
Makinen, who said he had misjudged a corner, was unhurt.
The stage was scrapped after another Finn, Jarmo Kytolehto, crashed his Ford within sight of the start.
Former world title-holder Colin McRae of Britain held a four seconds lead over Italy's Piero Liatti at the end of the first day. Both men were driving Subarus.
After a disappointing, accident-ridden season, McRae kept his cool on the long, abrasive stages that shredded the tyres of rival cars.
McRae was not concerned that he must now open the roads on Tuesday's second leg. "There's not so much mileage tomorrow and the tyres are working well. It's looking good," he said.
Didier Auriol, another ex-world champion, has gradually come to terms with his car on his first rally for Mitsubishi.
"I'm in a good position and I'm pleased after such a long break and driving a car I don't know," said the sixth-placed Frenchman.
